solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of Kurdistan that’s remote

indicators.note: only a part of the region's name is wanted, so the answer sits inside the word 'Kurdistan' and the next word

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the place name and into the next word

explanation.surface: A geography note about a far-flung corner of the Kurdish homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: KurDISTAN That's holds DISTANT; the apostrophe-s is part of the link, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying far away from here is described with this plain adjective, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Frustrated duke is given a job

blocks.note: someone given a post has been named to it

explanation.surface: A thwarted nobleman is finally handed some employment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'frustrated' with 'duke' as if describing him; in fact 'Frustrated' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let down when hopes fail is a common synonym for having plans or wishes thwarted.

clue.text: South of us, loch shows acidity

blocks.note: the famous Scottish lake, home of the legendary monster

explanation.surface: A travel remark about a Scottish lake lying south of the speakers, oddly revealing something acidic.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is the Scottish lake of monster fame, so 'loch' gives NESS; 'South of us' reads as a location but is S plus OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, tart quality in taste is the synonym here, the same property chemists call acidity.

clue.text: Creative pronunciation of radio talker’s introductions

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their opening letters, taken from 'radio' and 'talker'
we are told to say the two chosen letters out loud and hear a word

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the two words
the two letter names said one after the other

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's inventive way of saying the words that open their show.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter names 'ar' and 'tee' said together make ARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing artistic pretensions or flair, an informal synonym for being imaginative and inventive.

clue.text: Vibration of vacant tower Italian city erected

indicators.note: a vacant thing has had its insides emptied, so only the outside letters of 'tower' stay
in a down clue, putting the city upright means writing it from bottom to top

blocks.note: first and last letters of the building

explanation.surface: Shaking felt from an empty tower being put up in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian city erected' suggests a tower being built there; the city is Rome, flipped in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight shaking movement, such as a small earthquake, is a direct synonym of this quivering motion.

clue.text: Atmosphere of mixed feelings after Val’s departure

indicators.note: once Val has left, those three letters are taken out of the feelings word

blocks.note: the state of feeling two ways about something

explanation.surface: The mood in a room of conflicted emotions once someone called Val has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram signal, but 'mixed feelings' is a phrase for AMBIVALENCE, from which VAL is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The character or mood that a place gives off is a synonym for its general feel or setting.

clue.text: Leaders in Sunday Times editions transmit editor’s instruction

indicators.note: the leaders of a line of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Newspaper editorials in a Sunday paper send out a directive from the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' also means newspaper editorials, which fits the Sunday Times surface; here it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'let it stand', marked by proofreaders to cancel a correction and keep original wording.

clue.text: Repeat of contest about lighter alternative?

blocks.note: you can strike one instead of using a cigarette lighter

explanation.surface: A second bout fought over which is better, a lighter or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' reads as less heavy, but it is the gadget for lighting; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A second game or fight between the same opponents is exactly a contest held again.

clue.text: Conceptual policy that he developed

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words used as letters

explanation.surface: A theoretical programme that some man drew up.
explanation.walkthrough: All twelve letters of 'policy that he' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing only as an idea or supposition rather than in reality; both words describe theoretical, untested notions.

clue.text: Short-route transport is closed and let out

indicators.note: 'out' can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters of 'let' are jumbled

blocks.note: a closed door is one that is not open

explanation.surface: A transport link that has been shut down and then allowed to run again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' looks like one phrase meaning released; 'out' is working alone on 'let'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus, train or plane running back and forth over a short fixed route is called this.

clue.text: Mother keen on Papa’s platform on a ship

blocks.note: being into something means being enthusiastic about it
P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mum is fond of Dad's favourite spot aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papa' pairs with 'Mother' as a parent, but it is the radio alphabet word for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for the platform at the head of the lower mainmast of a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Joke using ambiguity, primarily known for rebellious style?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of 'known' is taken

explanation.surface: A wisecrack famed for its defiant attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Known for' reads as one phrase; 'primarily known' supplies a letter and 'for' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The anti-establishment 1970s music and fashion movement, with safety pins and mohicans, is one example of rebel style.

clue.text: On drugs — or a clothes line?

blocks.note: slang for being addicted to or high on narcotics
washing hung in a row along a cord, spread out along its length

explanation.surface: A choice between a high and a row of laundry, asked in one breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: garments on a washing line are pegged out in a row. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for addicted or intoxicated by narcotics, and literally stretched along in a line like pegged laundry.

clue.text: Scene one: note sailor’s curved sword

blocks.note: third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A stage direction: in the opening scene a sailor's cutlass is noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scene one' looks like a script heading and 'note' like 'notice'; they are SC, I and the sol-fa MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sabre with a strongly curved blade, associated with the Middle East, is this named weapon.

clue.text: Protective clothing completed start of Shakespeare comedy

blocks.note: first word of the title All's Well That Ends Well

explanation.surface: Workwear that was finished at the opening of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' is not a first letter here: it is the first word of the play All's Well That Ends Well.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn over ordinary clothes to keep them clean at work is a kind of protective wear.

clue.text: Prompt AI, setting anagrams

indicators.note: used as a verb, the clue tells us that the preceding words get rearranged

blocks.note: the two words used as letters

explanation.surface: A computer program is given a prompt and sets puzzles, a nod to AI-made crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' in the AI sense is an instruction to a chatbot; here it is a verb meaning to spur on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or set something going, as in to provoke or incite an action, is this verb.

clue.text: First man with Rear Admiral raised fleet of warships

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the pieces up means reading them from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer and his first mate assemble a battle fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's first man and the rank abbreviation are joined, then the whole string is turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A large naval force, most famously the Spanish one of 1588, is a group of fighting vessels.

clue.text: Humorist secures right legal document

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the humorist holds 'right' inside

explanation.surface: A comedian obtains the rights to a piece of legal paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside WIT, splitting it after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written court order commanding someone to act or refrain is a kind of official legal paper.

clue.text: Doctor or I must travel

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words used as letters

explanation.surface: A physician insisting that either they or the speaker has to go on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun, a physician; it is the imperative verb meaning alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Visiting places for pleasure is the business and activity of holidaymaking, here clued by a general noun.

clue.text: Druggie’s trick, putting the head all the way down

indicators.text: putting the head all the way down
indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter of 'trick' is moved to the very bottom

explanation.surface: An addict's stunt of lowering their head right to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of RUSE drops to the end, leaving USER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes illegal substances regularly is informally called this, a slang synonym for an addict.

clue.text: Slavic man’s first person to become Republican

explanation.surface: An Eastern European man is the first to switch to the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' is grammar, I, not a pioneer; 'go' means become as in 'go red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian given name, so an example of a male name from a Slavic country.

clue.text: Wacky Ealing comedy’s opening is very innocent

indicators.note: something wacky is crazy and disordered, so the letters of the studio name are jumbled
the opening of the word 'comedy' is its first letter

explanation.surface: The start of a madcap Ealing film proves utterly harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios made classic British comedies such as The Ladykillers; the name plus C is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Like an angel, pure and good; an extended sense meaning blameless, sweet and without any sin.

clue.text: Obstinately reactionary daughter that is difficult

blocks.note: abbreviation of the Latin id est

explanation.surface: A stubborn, old-fashioned daughter who is hard to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' becomes i.e., the abbreviation for id est.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly resisting change and clinging to old views; describes a hardliner or traditionalist who never yields.

clue.text: Look back on turbulent sea or spray

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of 'sea or' are stirred
going back means reading the word for 'look' from right to left

blocks.note: the two words used as letters

explanation.surface: Gazing back over a rough sea or the flying spray.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the reversed LO follows the rearranged 'sea or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressurised can releasing a fine mist, or the mist itself, is this kind of dispenser.
